title: pH/EC Meter Verification, Calibration & Sample Quality

content.overview: A precise digital display is not proof of an accurate measurement. pH and EC decisions depend on suitable standards, probe condition, sample handling, temperature effects and traceable calibration/verification records.

vocabulary.definition: A reference solution with a known value used to verify or calibrate a measurement device.
Physical and chemical state of the sensing element, including cleanliness, storage and damage.
Confidence that the measured sample is correctly identified, representative and handled appropriately.

sections.title: Consistency is not accuracy
sections.body: A meter can repeat the same wrong result. Failed verification against appropriate standards should be resolved before process changes depend on the reading.

sections.title: Probe and sample condition matter
sections.body: Residue, poor storage, temperature differences, contamination or mislabeled samples can create misleading measurements even when the meter was recently calibrated.

sections.title: Preserve questionable measurements
sections.body: Flag and investigate suspect results instead of deleting or rewriting them to match expectation.

workedExamples: Two recently calibrated meters disagree substantially on the same sample; verify standards, probe condition, sample identity and temperature context before using either value for correction.
commonMistakes: Trusting repeatability as proof of accuracy.
Changing chemistry before confirming the measurement system.
content.practicalApplication: Create a pH/EC meter-control log with device ID, standards, verification result, cleaning, probe condition and response to failure.
content.summary: Water-quality control is only as reliable as the measurement system and sample integrity.
